title: fix: class C keeps a seat dir holding a nested live worktree, and backs a failed evidence move
body:
Class C of `tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh` (the orphaned-seat sweep) deleted
what its own header promised to keep: an orphaned seat directory containing
a NESTED registered live worktree was `rm -rf`'d wholesale, in the same run
that printed `keep .../open-wt  open-pr` for that very worktree — the guard
(`another_live_under`) existed but was wired only into `dispose_seat_dir`
(classes A/B). Secondary gap in the same class: a failed evidence `mv` did
not backstop class C's removal, where A/B keep the seat. Both are #1288,
found post-merge by #1287's reviewer (verdict comment `d5acaa2`, attack 1).

The fix wires the guard into class C's eligibility — `live_under()` now
prints the live worktree under a seat dir (`another_live_under()` is its
non-empty test, one implementation instead of two), and the keep reason
line NAMES the nested worktree — and gives class C the failed-move
backstop: a leftover `evidence*`/`ev-*` dir after `preserve_evidence`
keeps the seat under `dispose_seat_dir`'s own `nondisposable-contents`
rule. Two new self-test case classes pin both shapes. SAFETY: the tool
deletes files; every run below executed inside the self-test's or the
attack harness's sandboxed fixtures (both redirect
`WORKTREE_GC_SEATS_ROOT`/`WORKTREE_GC_TMP_ROOT` into a mktemp dir; the
suite's own null control asserts the real `/tmp/hpo-orch` is never
walked). The real sweep was never invoked.

Closes #1288.

## Head

2a88b6b0ad8a99ef208b297f1bf75ee3995297aa (branch `fix/gc-class-c`, one
commit over origin/main at 2de1c182334e127748f518c72d8c54cd82020b59,
the merge of #1287). All figures below measured at this tree,
2026-09-20 16:57 UTC. Evidence logs: `/tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-1288/evidence-fix/`.

## Mutation proof

Both mutations delete the fix's own predicate lines in class C (not tail
appends), run `bash tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh --self-test`, and are
restored; the restored tree is byte-identical to the committed head
(`cmp` against the snapshot taken before mutating).

- Mutation A — delete class C's `live_under` wiring (the `nested=$(live_under ...)`
  keep block): `worktree_gc self-test: 66 checks, 5 failed`, rc 1. Red:
  `the nested LIVE worktree is not deleted`, `and the seat dir holding it
  is kept`, `kept naming the nested worktree`, `never announced as an
  orphan removal (null control)`, `the live worktree's file is intact`.
  Log: `evidence-fix/mutation-A.log`.
- Mutation B — delete class C's failed-move backstop loop: `worktree_gc
  self-test: 66 checks, 3 failed`, rc 1. Red: `the evidence stays in the
  seat dir`, `and the seat dir is kept`, `kept naming
  nondisposable-contents`. Log: `evidence-fix/mutation-B.log`.
- Restored: `worktree_gc self-test: 66 checks, 0 failed`, rc 0.

These are the two mutation pairs the self-test's header comment says the
carrying pull request records.

## Null control

The unmodified tree at 2de1c18: the committed self-test reports
`worktree_gc self-test: 54 checks, 0 failed` (rc 0) — that is the detector
gap itself — while the reviewer's attack harness reproduces the deletion:
`FAIL attack1: nested LIVE open-PR worktree under an orphaned seat dir
(got 'DELETED', want 'kept')` and `FAIL attack1: the seat dir holding it
(got 'REMOVED', want 'kept')`, `attack harness: 11 checks, 2 failed`, rc 1.
With the two new case classes added to that unmodified tree (failing
first): `worktree_gc self-test: 66 checks, 8 failed`, rc 1 — exactly the 5
nested-live and 3 failed-move checks; all 54 pre-existing checks green
before and after. The base+cases state is reconstructed deterministically
(HEAD minus the three production edits); stripping the new cases from it
yields a file byte-identical to `git show origin/main:tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh`.

Attack-harness adaptation, disclosed: the reviewer's
`/tmp/hpo-orch/review-1287/attack.sh` re-run verbatim except line 7
(`SELF_TOOL`) repointed at the tool under test — base copy for the
"before" arm, the worktree copy at the head SHA for the "after" arm;
`diff` of the two harnesses shows only that line. At the head:
`attack harness: 11 checks, 0 failed`, rc 0 — attack 1 now prints
`keep .../orch/seat-live  live-worktree (.../orch/seat-live/open-wt)`
and the summary reads `eligible 0, removed 0, kept 3`. Attacks 1b, 2 and
3 (the arms the #1287 verdict already verified) stay green.

## Figures

Rule for every check count below: it is the self-test's own summary line
(its `st` invocations), not a recount; rc is the shell's.

- `bash /tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-1288/attack/worktree_gc.base.sh --self-test`
  (that file is `git show origin/main:tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh`)
  → `worktree_gc self-test: 54 checks, 0 failed`, rc 0.
- `bash /tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-1288/selftest-base-newcases.sh --self-test`
  → `worktree_gc self-test: 66 checks, 8 failed`, rc 1 (failing first).
- `bash tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh --self-test`
  → `worktree_gc self-test: 66 checks, 0 failed`, rc 0 (at head; log
  `evidence-fix/selftest-head.log`).
- `bash /tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-1288/evidence-fix/attack-adapted.sh` with
  `SELF_TOOL` at the base copy → `attack harness: 11 checks, 2 failed`,
  rc 1; at the head copy → `attack harness: 11 checks, 0 failed`, rc 0
  (logs `attack-base.log`, `attack-head.log`).
- Gate scope: `D=$(mktemp -d); python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D" | grep 'MODE:'`
  → `MODE: SCOPED -- 0 script(s) run, 24 scoped out.`; `scope.run` names
  nothing, so nothing is run locally (the file is INERT under
  `tools/audit/`; `tests/entities.py`'s orphan check keeps that list
  honest and passed). Log: `evidence-fix/closure-select.log`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/structure.py` → rc 0
  (`STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`); same invocation for `tests/entities.py`
  → rc 0 (`ALL 1630 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`) and `tests/harness_headers.py`
  → rc 0 (`ALL 91 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED` — no EXPECTED header pins
  this script's output, so none moved).
- Claim files: `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD --stat -- tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt && echo IDENTICAL`
  → `IDENTICAL` (empty diff; the branch claims nothing).
- Changed files: `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD --name-only`
  → `tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh` only.

## Red checks

The defect reached main inside #1287 (merged at bc8365f; the blocked
verdict landed post-merge). The check that stayed green while the
property was violated is the tool's own self-test — 54 checks, 0 failed —
because its nested-live-worktree case existed only for the class A/B side
(attack 1b), never for class C. Cheaper detector: the two case classes
added here — the same harness, no new instrument; standing cost: 12 more
checks (54 → 66) in a self-test that runs in seconds beside every §11
call. No gate check turns red on this branch: the scoped gate runs zero
scripts, and structure, entities and harness_headers are rc 0 above; CI
re-executes them on push. Root-cause analysis is not this seat's
(`briefs/root-cause.md` runs beside a fix, never inside it); the trigger
is named here per `defect-root-cause.md`.

## Forward-carry

none — the tool's caller contract (`briefs/orchestrator.md` §11) is
unchanged, no later stage's behavior depends on class C's internal
guards, and the finding already reached this seat through #1287's verdict
and #1288. The self-test header's "mutation pairs recorded in the pull
request that carried this file" is discharged by this body's Mutation
proof section.

## Friction

none
